output.brief:
The wrong dates did not come from the operators or the printer upgrade. Printer records show every Veltranol job from 2 June to 3 October used a 24-month shelf life and printed correctly, including the post-upgrade jobs run by the new agency staff. From 4 October the data sent to the printers said 36 months, and the printers printed exactly what they received. No operator overrides occurred. The ERP shows Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months on 3 October for lots made from March 2027, but the system still delivered it to the line. The two later Veltranol jobs on Line 1 day shift, run by permanent staff, are now in the warehouse. The director's plan would punish the wrong people and leave the fault in place. The camera only checks print against the job, so it is working as designed and should stay on.

Do now: fix the Veltranol shelf-life records so only 24 months can be read. Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 October, including the two warehouse lots. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup. Check retained cartons of other products edited in October, especially the two with future-dated changes. Find out why the future-dated value was used. I'm fairly confident in this, though other products remain unchecked.
